item.title: SK Hynix broke ground on its first U.S. AI chip packaging plant in Indiana
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 5.06
SK Hynix held a groundbreaking ceremony on Thursday for an advanced chip packaging facility in West Lafayette, Indiana, marking the South Korean chipmaker's first high-bandwidth memory production base in the United States. The South Korean chipmaker plans to begin mass production of next-generation HBM chips at the West Lafayette facility in the third quarter of 2029 The facility, located at Purdue Research Park, represents a total investment of more than $4 billion. SK Hynix plans to open the cleanroom by October 2028 and begin volume production of its next-generation HBM4E chips in the third quarter of 2029, according to Reuters. The company said the plant is designed to support a workforce of around 1,000 people when it reaches full capacity, while the overall investment is projected to sustain roughly 7,000 jobs in total when construction, ongoing operations, and supplier activity are counted together. Rather than fabricating chips from scratch, the Indiana facility will receive DRAM wafers manufactured in South Korea and carry out the stacking, packaging, and testing steps needed to turn them into finished HBM products for American customers. SK Hynix CEO Kwak Noh-Jung told attendees that the Indiana plant is being designed to handle annual throughput in the hundreds of thousands of wafers. Counterpoint Research data cited by Reuters shows SK Hynix held a 58% share of global HBM revenue in the first quarter of 2026. Kwak told reporters he has not observed meaningful indicators of a coming memory cycle decline, and that if conditions soften, he anticipates a gradual deceleration rather than a steep drop in demand. The company's major customers for HBM include Nvidia $NVDA, Microsoft $MSFT, and Alphabet $GOOGL's Google. Under the CHIPS and Science Act, the U.S. government committed to offering the company as much as $458 million in direct funding along with $500 million in loans, SK Hynix said. According to Korea Herald, work at the approximately 540,000-square-meter site actually got underway in April, well before the formal ceremony, and steel frames are already visible above ground. At the ceremony, SK Hynix signed a memorandum of understanding with Purdue University covering joint research on advanced packaging technologies, including HBM. The company also said it plans to recruit engineering talent from across the Midwest through the partnership. Indiana Governor Mike Braun and U.S. Senator Todd Young of Indiana attended the ceremony alongside South Korean Ambassador to the U.S. Kang Kyung-wha and SK Hynix executives. "This project will create good-paying jobs, strengthen our national and economic security, and ensure the technologies of the future are developed and manufactured here in the United States," Senator Young said in a statement. SK Hynix's CEO predicted earlier this year that 2027 would bring the most severe memory supply crunch the industry has ever seen, with customer demand running ahead of the company's production capacity well beyond 2030. The Indiana investment is part of a broader SK Group commitment that is expected to put total U.S. investments and assets above $45 billion by 2030, SK Inc. Vice Chairman Yu Jeong-joon said at the ceremony. Join 500,000+ readers who start their day with Quartz. By subscribing, you agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

item.title: The safest baby bottles of 2026, according to Consumer Reports
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 4.93
The safest baby bottles of 2026, according to Consumer Reports Baby bottles can leach chemicals under certain conditions. Consumer Reports tested nine popular options for safety concerns A baby's small body is especially vulnerable to chemicals like bisphenol A, lead and phthalates, substances that can sometimes leach out of feeding products. Material choice matters here, since glass and food-grade silicone are less likely than plastic to contain these chemicals, and high heat can cause a plastic bottle to release any BPA it does contain. Consumer Reports tested nine popular baby bottles made from plastic, silicone and glass for BPA, lead and eight different phthalates, so parents can see exactly which options passed. Dr. Brown's Natural Flow Anti-Colic Options+ Credit: Amazon Priced at $5, the Dr. Brown's Natural Flow Anti-Colic Options+ is made of glass, the material specifically recommended among the bottles tested for reducing lead exposure risk. Consumer Reports found no BPA, lead or any of the eight phthalates tested for in this bottle. CR found glass carries a much lower chance of containing bisphenols or phthalates in the first place compared with plastic, though breakage is the tradeoff to watch for. Testers noted lead contamination in baby bottles is uncommon but unpredictable, since there's no way to know a specific product is lead-free without testing it directly. Boon Nursh Silicone Baby Bottle Credit: Amazon The Boon Nursh Silicone Baby Bottle costs $10 and uses a collapsible silicone pouch design. Consumer Reports detected none of the eight phthalates tested for, nor BPA or lead, in this bottle. CR found food-grade silicone, like glass, is less likely than plastic to contain bisphenols or phthalates. Testers noted silicone bottles avoid the high-heat concerns tied to plastic, since they don't carry the same risk of releasing BPA when heated. Comotomo Natural Feel Credit: Amazon The Comotomo Natural Feel costs $12 and is made entirely from silicone. Consumer Reports's testing turned up no trace of BPA, lead or the eight phthalates it screened for in this bottle. CR found silicone bottles generally carry a lower risk of containing these chemicals compared with plastic. Testers said choosing silicone or glass over plastic is one of the more effective ways to reduce a baby's chemical exposure risk. Green Sprouts Silicone & Sprout Ware Baby Pocket Credit: Amazon At $18, the Green Sprouts Silicone & Sprout Ware Baby Pocket costs more than every other bottle in this test. Consumer Reports found this bottle free of BPA, lead and all eight phthalates included in its testing panel. CR found this bottle's silicone construction carries the same reduced-risk profile as the other silicone and glass bottles tested. Testers noted researchers are still tracking newer replacement chemicals, such as BPS and BPF, that manufacturers sometimes substitute for BPA, even though CR didn't test this bottle for those specific compounds. Lansinoh Baby Bottle Credit: Amazon Made of plastic, the $7 Lansinoh Baby Bottle is one of five plastic bottles included in this test. Consumer Reports tested this bottle for BPA, lead and eight phthalates, and found none of them present. CR found high heat, such as a microwave or dishwasher cycle, could still cause a plastic bottle to release BPA if it were present, even though none was detected here. Testers recommended hand-washing plastic bottles with a bottle brush and air-drying them instead of running them through a dishwasher. Mam Anti-Colic Baby Bottle Credit: Amazon The $6 Mam Anti-Colic Baby Bottle is made of plastic, like most other bottles in this test. Consumer Reports screened this bottle for BPA, lead and eight phthalates, and came up empty on all three fronts. CR found overheating milk or formula inside a plastic bottle is another situation worth avoiding for the same reason. Testers noted manufacturers sometimes replace BPA with related compounds like BPS or BPF, which weren't part of this specific test. Nuk Smooth Flow Baby Bottle Credit: Amazon Plastic construction defines the $6 Nuk Smooth Flow Baby Bottle. Consumer Reports's lab analysis found this bottle contained no BPA, lead or any of the eight phthalates it tested for. CR found microplastics are a separate concern tied to plastic bottles generally, distinct from the chemical compounds tested for here. Testers said switching to glass or silicone remains an option for parents who want to avoid plastic altogether. Philips Avent Natural Baby Bottle Credit: Amazon The $10 Philips Avent Natural Baby Bottle uses a plastic build. Consumer Reports found this bottle passed its screening for BPA, lead and eight separate phthalates without a single detection. CR found federal regulations limit the use of the eight phthalates tested for, though many related compounds outside that specific list still exist on the market. Testers noted researchers believe cumulative exposure to many different phthalate types, not just a handful, may be what drives related health concerns. Tommee Tippee Closer to Nature Baby Bottle Credit: Amazon Rounding out the plastic bottles in this test, the $6 Tommee Tippee Closer to Nature Baby Bottle costs the same as several other options evaluated. Consumer Reports found no evidence of BPA, lead or the eight phthalates it tested for in this bottle. CR found complete avoidance of chemical exposure is nearly impossible given how widespread contamination has become, according to one researcher CR consulted. Testers said public health regulation, not individual shopping choices alone, is ultimately what experts believe is needed to meaningfully reduce these exposures.

item.title: Novo Nordisk is seeking Chinese approval for its oral weight loss pill
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 4.87
China's drug regulator accepted Novo Nordisk's application for an oral version of Wegovy as the Danish company competes with Eli Lilly in the market Novo Nordisk launched the Wegovy pill in the U.S. this year after receiving approval there and in Britain. Novo Nordisk has offered no indication of when Chinese approval might come. "We respect the regulatory review process and therefore we are not able to offer information on potential approval timelines," the company said in a statement to Reuters. Eli Lilly moved first in China. The U.S. drugmaker submitted a marketing application for its once-daily oral weight loss pill, orforglipron, to the Chinese regulator at the end of 2025. Lilly secured U.S. approval for orforglipron in April, and a company executive said the drug could reach the Chinese market before the end of this year. Both Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly belong to a group of competitors — which also includes Pfizer $PFE and local firm Innovent Biologics — vying for market share in China's weight loss drug sector. According to China's National Health Commission, the share of overweight or obese people in the country could top 65% by 2030, the company said. Both Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly believe oral pills could attract patients who are reluctant to use injections. Both oral drugs are GLP-1 therapies, a class that works by replicating the action of a naturally occurring gut hormone, suppressing hunger and helping to keep blood sugar levels in check for people living with diabetes. item.title: The most comfortable shoe insoles, according to Consumer Reports
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 4.79
The most comfortable shoe insoles, according to Consumer Reports Shoe inserts can feel supportive to one foot type and awkward to another. Consumer Reports had a panel test four options for comfort and fitc Shoe inserts promise extra arch support and cushioning, but what feels supportive to one foot can feel awkward or unstable to another. Arch height, cushioning material and how easily an insert fits into a shoe without trimming can determine whether an insole actually gets worn. Consumer Reports had a panel of testers with different foot types try four shoe inserts over several weeks, so shoppers can find one suited to their own feet. PowerStep Pinnacle Insoles Credit: Amazon Priced at $49.95, the PowerStep Pinnacle Insoles feature dual-layer cushioning and an odor-control top fabric, and come in separate men's and women's sizing. Consumer Reports named this its top pick overall for comfort, fit and stability, and one male tester said he felt noticeably steadier and stood straighter after wearing them. CR found the arch support felt overly pronounced at first for that same tester, though it grew more comfortable the longer he wore the insoles. Testers said the insoles fit right into their shoes with no trimming required, and female testers unanimously named these their favorite of all the inserts evaluated. Stepprs Massage Insoles Credit: Amazon The Stepprs Massage Insoles cost $42 and use raised bumps across a memory foam surface, which the manufacturer says can be trimmed to fit and hand-washed. Consumer Reports named this its runner-up pick, and testers described the massage-bump sensation as unusual at first but soothing once they got used to it. CR found the manufacturer claims these insoles should last more than 12 months with normal use. Testers with bunions preferred the PowerStep Pinnacle to this pick, noting the raised bumps seemed to create a tighter fit around the forefoot. WalkHero Inserts Credit: Amazon The WalkHero Inserts cost $15.98 and include 3.5 centimeters of arch support, notably higher than the other inserts evaluated. Consumer Reports found opinions split sharply along foot type, with one tester who has high arches saying these felt right from the first step. CR found a tester with flat feet considered them functional but lacking the firmer arch structure and steadiness he typically looks for in an insole. Testers with bunions said their feet felt positioned too high, and one needed to trim the insert with scissors before it fit her shoe comfortably. Dr. Scholl's Work All-Day Insoles Credit: Amazon The Dr. Scholl's Work All-Day Insoles cost $11.15, less than every other insole in this test, and come in separate men's and women's sizing. Consumer Reports named this its budget pick, though testers found the thinner material harder to insert without crumpling, and every tester ended up trimming the insoles with scissors to get a better fit. CR found most testers didn't consider the insoles supportive enough, despite appreciating the built-in massaging gel. Testers were split on comfort, with one calling the cushioning softer than any other insole he'd tried, even though it didn't feel as substantial as some competitors.

item.title: If You Invested $1000 in Morgan Stanley a Decade Ago, This is How Much It'd Be Worth Now
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 4.55
How much a stock's price changes over time is important for most investors, since price performance can both impact your investment portfolio and help you compare investment results across sectors and industries. Why investing for the long run, especially if you buy certain popular stocks, could reap huge rewards. Another thing that can drive investing is the fear of missing out, or FOMO. This particularly applies to tech giants and popular consumer-facing stocks. What if you'd invested in Morgan Stanley $MS (MS) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to MS for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today? With that in mind, let's take a look at Morgan Stanley's main business drivers. Founded in 1935 and incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware in 1981, Morgan Stanley is the leading financial services holding company headquartered in New York. With 82,944 employees as of June 30, 2026, the company serves a diversified group of clients and customers, including corporations, governments, financial institutions and individuals, through offices across 41 countries. The company’s business is divided into three segments: The Institutional Securities ("IS") segment (contributing 46.5% of total net revenues in 2025) includes capital raising; financial advisory services that include advices on mergers and acquisitions (M&As), restructurings, real estate and project finance; corporate lending; sales, trading, financing and market-making activities in equity and fixed income securities and related products, including foreign exchange and commodities; benchmark indices and risk management analytics; and investment activities. The Wealth Management ("WM") segment (44.4%) provides brokerage and investment advisory services covering various investment alternatives; financial and wealth planning services; annuity and other insurance products; credit and other lending products; cash management services; retirement services; and trust and fiduciary services and engages in fixed income principal trading. The Investment Management ("IM") segment (9%) provides global asset management products and services in equity, fixed income, alternative investments that include hedge funds and funds of funds, and merchant banking, including real estate, private equity and infrastructure, to institutional and retail clients through proprietary and third-party distribution channels. The segment also engages in investment. In 2019, Morgan Stanley acquired Canada-based Solium Capital Inc. and renamed it as Shareworks by Morgan Stanley. In 2020, the company acquired E*Trade Financial. In 2021, it acquired Eaton Vance. In January 2026, the company acquired EquityZen, a private shares marketplace. Anyone can invest, but building a successful investment portfolio requires research, patience, and a little bit of risk. So, if you had invested in Morgan Stanley, ten years ago, you're likely feeling pretty good about your investment today. According to our calculations, a $1000 investment made in August 2016 would be worth $6,870.35, or a gain of 587.03%, as of August 27, 2026, and this return excludes dividends but includes price increases. Compare this to the S&P 500's rally of 253.88% and gold's return of 234.25% over the same time frame. Analysts are forecasting more upside for MS too. Shares of Morgan Stanley have outperformed the industry in the past year, suggesting meaningful execution progress. Its earnings surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in the trailing four quarters. It benefits from a durable wealth and asset management franchise that supports steadier fee income and deep client relationships, with strategic alliances adding to long-term growth. The investment banking (IB) business will benefit from a healthier deal environment, supported by a robust and diversified pipeline. However, expense pressure from growth initiatives, technology spend and platform investments may limit operating leverage. Trading has been supportive, but the business is volatile and hard to grow from current levels. A premium valuation limits its upside potential. Nevertheless, a strong capital position allows continued shareholder returns. The stock has jumped 5.39% over the past four weeks. item.title: U.S. goods trade deficit hit its widest in 16 months as AI spending lifted imports
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 4.41
The U.S. goods trade deficit widened to $118.8 billion in July, up $17.4 billion from $101.4 billion in June, the Census Bureau reported Thursday. The reading represented the widest monthly goods deficit recorded since March 2025. Capital goods imports surged 11.3% as AI-driven equipment spending lifted total imports to $318.2 billion, while initial jobless claims fell to 203,000 Total imports climbed 3.7% to $318.2 billion, with capital goods accounting for much of the gain after that category surged 11.3%. On the other side of the ledger, exports dropped 2.9% to $199.4 billion, pulled down largely by a steep 11.2% contraction in industrial goods shipments. The expanding gap suggests trade will again subtract from gross domestic product growth, potentially marking a fourth straight quarter of such drag, according to Reuters. Matthew Martin, senior U.S. economist at Oxford Economics, attributed the capital goods surge to business spending on high-tech equipment tied to the AI investment boom. "We expect capital goods imports to support strong growth in imports well into 2027," Martin said. In a separate release Thursday, the Labor Department reported that first-time unemployment filings dropped by 4,000, settling at a seasonally adjusted 203,000 through the week ended August 22. The result came in below the 208,000 that economists surveyed by Reuters had anticipated. The four-week moving average for initial claims rose 1,250 to 205,500. Continuing claims — a proxy for hiring — shed 18,000 to reach a seasonally adjusted 1.778 million in the period ended August 15. The insured unemployment rate held at 1.2%. As recently as the prior week's report, initial claims had totaled 206,000, with continuing claims rising to 1,799,000 for the week ending August 8. Thursday's data showed improvement on both measures. Thomas Simons, chief U.S. economist at Jefferies, said recent payroll processor and labor market data "paint a picture of a labor market that is in better balance" than official figures suggest. "There is a modest, steady pace of private sector job creation that is right in line with the amount necessary to keep the unemployment rate steady," Simons said. Throughout 2026, initial claims have oscillated between 189,000 and 230,000, a pattern that points to a labor market where job losses have stayed limited despite a slowdown in new hiring. item.title: The Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic was unconstitutional, judge rules
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 4.38
A federal judge ruled Thursday that the Pentagon's effort to blacklist Anthropic violated the First Amendment and the due process clause of the Fifth Amendment, and ordered the government to rescind all directives issued against the AI company. A federal judge set aside the supply chain risk designation that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had placed on the AI startup U.S. District Judge Rita Lin of the Northern District of California found that officials had retaliated against Anthropic in violation of the First Amendment and had stripped the company of liberty interests without adequate notice or a meaningful chance to respond. "The empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics," Lin wrote in her 59-page opinion. Lin set aside the supply chain risk designation that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had placed on Anthropic and issued a permanent injunction barring the government from giving effect to the challenged actions. She further ordered the Department of Defense and other named agencies to pull back every internal directive and communication put in place to carry out the designation. The ruling found that the government's rationale rested principally on Anthropic's public criticism of the administration's views on AI. "Neither the Constitution nor the federal statute invoked by Defendants allows them to impose sweeping penalties based principally on Anthropic's critique of the Administration's views," Lin wrote. Anthropic said in a statement that it was "pleased the court has ruled that this supply chain risk designation was unlawful," adding that it looks forward to continuing to partner with federal agencies to advance AI capabilities in service of national security. The conflict between Anthropic and the Trump administration grew out of a $200 million contract dispute over how the Pentagon could deploy the company's Claude AI models on classified systems. Anthropic pushed for contractual limits barring use of its models in autonomous lethal weapons systems or domestic mass surveillance, a position the Defense Department rejected on the grounds that corporate contractors have no authority to dictate military operating rules. When negotiations broke down, Hegseth designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk — a formal status historically reserved for foreign entities considered threats to national security — effectively cutting off every Pentagon contractor and supplier from doing business with the company. Anthropic filed two separate lawsuits in March in response to the blacklisting, one in California and a parallel case in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit, the latter required because the DOD grounded its action in two distinct designations. Thursday's order does not require the Defense Department to use Anthropic's products, and it does not bar the government from transitioning to other AI providers, provided those actions comply with applicable law. item.title: Synopsys posted strong earnings and raised its outlook but its stock slipped anyway
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 4.04
Synopsys $SNPS reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $2.477 billion and raised its full-year guidance on Wednesday, though shares dropped 4% in after-hours trading despite the better-than-expected numbers, according to Seeking Alpha. The chip design software company reported $2.48 billion in quarterly revenue and lifted its full-year revenue target to $9.715 billion at the midpoint Revenue for the quarter ending July 31 rose from $1.740 billion in the same period a year earlier, the company said. On a GAAP basis, net income came in at $545.8 million, or $2.84 per diluted share, compared with $242.5 million, or $1.50 per diluted share, in the year-ago quarter. On a non-GAAP basis, earnings per diluted share were $3.91, up from $3.39 a year earlier — exceeding the high end of the company's prior guidance. The Design Automation segment, which includes electronic design automation software and Ansys products, generated $2.003 billion in revenue, accounting for roughly 81% of total revenue for the quarter. The Design IP segment brought in $473.8 million. Synopsys raised its full-year revenue target to a range of $9.690 billion to $9.740 billion, with a midpoint of $9.715 billion, the company said. It also lifted its full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to a range of $15.04 to $15.10, with a midpoint of $15.07. For the fourth quarter ending October 31, the company is targeting revenue of $2.530 billion to $2.580 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $4.10 to $4.16. "Synopsys delivered an outstanding third quarter, with revenue and earnings per share exceeding the high end of our guidance range," Chief Financial Officer Shelagh Glaser said in a statement. "Given our strong performance and expectations for double-digit growth in EDA, we are raising our full year revenue, non-GAAP operating margin, EPS and cash flow guidance." President and CEO Sassine Ghazi attributed the results to demand driven by artificial intelligence. "AI is driving unprecedented complexity and increasing demand for the silicon IP and engineering solutions necessary to deliver next-generation AI compute, infrastructure and physical AI systems," Ghazi said in a statement. "One year after the transformational acquisition of Ansys, we are executing with focus, extending our leadership and gaining momentum." Full-year guidance assumes no further changes to export control restrictions or current U.S. government Entity List restrictions, the company said. item.title: Alabama-Coushatta opens temporary Naskila Casino as permanent resort takes shape nearby
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Score: 4.70
The Alabama-Coushatta Tribe of Texas has opened Naskila Casino Leggett, giving Polk County its first operating piece of a much larger casino resort planned for the property. Tribal members marked the occasion Monday (August 24) with a Tribal Membership Opening Day ceremony. Doors opened to everyone Tuesday and visitors began lining up early. Operating around the clock, the temporary casino offers 300 electronic gaming machines and a dining facility. Local reporting says the operation has brought roughly 100 new jobs to the area. For tribal leaders, Leggett also signals a new period of economic development after years spent fighting in court over gaming. In 2022, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that Texas could not apply its gaming laws to stop electronic bingo on tribal land when state law did not prohibit the activity outright. Texas later abandoned its longstanding lawsuit against the Tribe. Naskila Casino Leggett opening signals wider tribal gaming and economic expansion Construction is already underway nearby on the permanent Naskila Casino Resort, which broke ground in June. Plans cover roughly 685,000 square feet, with about 3,400 electronic bingo machines and a 366-room hotel. Guests are also expected to find restaurants, bars and lounges, a resort-style pool complex and around 35,000 square feet for conferences and events. A grand ballroom is designed for crowds of up to 1,000 people. The opening of the first phase is targeted for late 2028. The development builds on Naskila’s existing operation near Livingston, which has been running since 2016. Tribal officials point to its wider role in the East Texas economy, including jobs and spending with regional businesses. An economic-impact study cited by the Tribe put that contribution at about $251.7 million annually. Federal agencies had previously confirmed the Leggett property could host gaming. The land has been held in trust since 2001, and tribal membership approved the location in September 2025. The federal status stands in contrast with another current tribal gaming dispute. In California, the Scotts Valley Band of Pomo Indians sued the Interior Department on August 7 after officials reversed their position on gaming eligibility for roughly 160 acres in Vallejo. Interior had approved that property in January 2025 as “restored lands” under federal gaming law, using broader readings of “occupancy” and “vicinity”. After another review, the department reversed course July 30. Scotts Valley called that decision “arbitrary, capricious, contrary to law, unsupported by the administrative record” and said it was “compelled to suspend gaming operations” at its Class II facility. The tribe had pursued a temporary “preview casino” while the dispute continued. In Leggett, meanwhile, the temporary casino is operating while construction moves ahead. The Alabama-Coushatta Tribe called its membership celebration “a new chapter” as it prepared to welcome the wider public. Featured image: Alabama-Coushatta Tribe of Texas via Facebook

item.title: Polymarket military bets expose security risks as soldier case reaches court
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Score: 2.49
More than 150 cryptocurrency wallets betting on military events through Polymarket behaved in ways researchers associate with possible insider trading. Now a separate federal prosecution involving a U.S. Army master sergeant is giving those concerns a real-world legal test. The Anti-Corruption Data Collective, or ACDC, identified 152 wallets making unusually successful longshot bets in military and defence markets. Together, the wallets won about $8 million. Its August report, Classifying Insider Trading Risk: Analyzing the Longshot Betting Ecosystem on Polymarket, examined 78,496 longshot bets from 12,355 wallets on markets settled through May 5, 2026. The research does not show that those 152 wallets belonged to military personnel, government officials or anyone else holding classified information. Instead, ACDC created a statistical profile for accounts whose behaviour resembles previously reported cases of suspected insider trading. Researchers call those accounts “Orcas.” They tend to focus on relatively few subjects, win unusually often when betting on outcomes the market considers unlikely and sometimes appear shortly before the event being predicted. ACDC put wallets with longshot success rates above 75%, concentrated activity and limited market breadth among its most suspicious accounts. Suspicious military bets appeared on Polymarket before larger traders moved in Of 1,432 wallets making longshot military bets, researchers classified 152 as Orcas. Another 482 were high-volume “Whales,” while 166 appeared to be automated Bots. The Orcas put roughly $2 million into military longshots and made an average profit of about $52,514 per wallet. ACDC cautioned that proving whether any individual trader actually possessed inside information would require investigative powers beyond the study. What happened after those bets appeared may be just as important. Around major military events, winning Orca wagers generally arrived before Whales and Bots moved into the same markets. “In both cases, longshot bets by Orcas preceded longshot bets by Whales and Bots,” the researchers found in their analysis of military-market activity. It raises the possibility that sophisticated traders were watching public blockchain transactions, spotting unusual bets and following them with larger positions. One informed wager could therefore become a signal that other market participants quickly amplify. “If financial speculators can quickly observe insider bets and act on them in real time, then so can militaries and intelligence agencies around the world,” the report says. ACDC examined activity surrounding Iran-related strikes in June 2025 and February 2026. During the June episode, an Orca made the first correct longshot wager more than a week before the strikes. Another bet about 13 hours before the attack was followed roughly 20 minutes later by a much larger Bot wager. In February, Orcas again appeared before Whales and Bots. Researchers saw a “flurry” of Orca activity around February 16, followed by increased Whale positions and more automated betting as the strikes approached. The pattern is consistent with other traders reacting to wallets they believed had better information, although it does not prove that explanation. Across the full dataset, ACDC classified 556 of the 12,355 longshot wallets as Orcas. The markets represented around $15.6 billion in betting volume and $197 million in net profits. Orcas averaged returns of 132% across all markets. Among those active in military markets, the report put average returns at about 167%, compared with roughly 1% for Whales and Bots and losses for ordinary traders labelled “Small Fish.” US soldier allegedly made $400,000 betting on classified operation The statistical warnings now sit alongside a separate criminal case in Manhattan involving Army Master Sgt. Gannon Ken Van Dyke, 38, who served with U.S. Army Special Operations Command at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. Federal prosecutors allege Van Dyke used classified and other nonpublic information he obtained through his work on Operation Absolute Resolve to make Polymarket bets involving U.S. military action in Venezuela and Nicolas Maduro’s removal from power. “The core theory of the Indictment is that Van Dyke took information that he had pledged to keep confidential and, though he was duty-bound not to do so, he used it to make a personal profit,” prosecutors said. According to prosecutors, Van Dyke opened his Polymarket account on December 26, 2025. Between December 27 and January 2, he allegedly spent about $33,934 buying “YES” shares connected to Venezuela and Maduro while working on the operation. One position involved roughly 13,769 shares predicting Maduro would be out of power by January 31, 2026. Van Dyke allegedly paid about nine cents a share, a market price implying roughly a 9% probability. U.S. special forces captured Maduro and his wife in Caracas before dawn on January 3. Once the operation became public, several contracts settled at $1 per “YES” share. Prosecutors allege Van Dyke made more than $400,000 in net profit. A federal grand jury indicted him in April on five counts involving confidential government information, commodities and swap fraud, wire fraud and an unlawful monetary transaction. Van Dyke pleaded not guilty and was released on $250,000 bail subject to travel restrictions. The Justice Department has described it as its first criminal insider-trading prosecution involving prediction markets. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission also filed a parallel civil case in April. Van Dyke asked the court on July 31 to dismiss the criminal indictment. Among his arguments, he contended that the event contracts were not swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act and that classified military information could not constitute property for wire-fraud purposes. Prosecutors pushed back in an August 19 filing in the Southern District of New York, arguing that all five counts should proceed and that Van Dyke’s arguments should be decided at trial. They say the statutory definition of swaps can cover event contracts with financial, economic or commercial consequences. They also cite Van Dyke’s nondisclosure obligations, including an agreement concerning “Western Hemisphere Operations” in which he acknowledged information obtained through his work “is now and will remain the property of the United States Government.” Van Dyke “committed an old crime on a new platform,” they said. “Because the Indictment alleges all that it must,” prosecutors said, “the next step is trial.” Public Polymarket trades could expose military secrets The Van Dyke allegations remain unproven, and the ACDC analysis separately stops well short of claiming that its 152 military-market Orcas possessed classified information. Together, though, the cases illustrate two sides of the same problem: identifying who may have traded on secret information and understanding what their public trades reveal to everybody else. Blockchain transparency helped ACDC follow funds through cryptocurrency exchanges, bridges, decentralised exchanges and other services. But public addresses do not necessarily disclose their owners, and trails can end at institutions handling assets for thousands of customers. That makes suspicious behavior easier to spot than the person responsible for it. The larger security concern can emerge before investigators ever identify a trader. Prediction markets covering wars, military operations and government decisions give people with confidential knowledge a financial incentive to act. Their wagers can then be monitored by algorithms, wealthy investors and potentially foreign intelligence services. ACDC recommends stronger bettor identification, conditional payouts for suspicious high-risk bets and restrictions on particularly vulnerable market categories. It ultimately argues that some markets present risks those measures cannot eliminate. “Only outright bans on the highest-risk market segments can adequately address the risks and the structural imbalance they sustain,” the report concludes. Whether any of ACDC’s 152 military-market wallets were controlled by people holding classified information remains unanswered. The Van Dyke prosecution could meanwhile test how existing fraud and commodities laws apply when prosecutors allege that government secrets were converted into prediction-market profits. The underlying vulnerability is broader than either case. Once secret knowledge becomes a publicly visible wager, other traders can see it, copy it and magnify it long before investigators determine who placed the original bet. Featured image: AI-generated image via Canva / Polymarket

item.title: Physical media rules: THE CARDBOARD LOVER (1928)
item.description:
Source: San Diego Reader stories Score: 5.67
THE CARDBOARD LOVER (1928) Robert Z. Leonard / Written by Lucille Newmark & Carey Wilson / Cinematography: John Arnold (1.33:1) / 2026 Musical Score Composed and Performed by Ben Model / Design: Cedric Gibbons / Editor: Basil Wrangell / Costumes: Howard Greer / Acted by: Marion Davies, Andrés de Segurola, Tenen Holta and Pepi Lederer / USA / An Undercrank Productions/Library of Congress Release of an M-G-M Picture / Length: 95 mins. A recent dive down an internet rabbit hole turned up some interesting inconsistencies regarding the The Cardboard Lover. The first thing I noticed was the variety of websites crediting it as the source material for a Buster Keaton picture. I’ve seen every scrap of film available starring the Great Stoneface, and for the life of me, I couldn’t connect the title with any of his shorts or features. Then I learned that The Passionate Plumber, a dismal Keaton talkie from 1932, was based on the play The Cardboard Lover. Frederick Lonsdale is frequently (and incorrectly) credited by various databases, IMDB among them, as the play's co-writer. The story of how Lonsdale became tangled up with it involves a mix of theatrical adaptation, Hollywood's penchant for remakes, and the classic studio system administrative blunders that followed. Credit for the original story belongs to French playwright Jacques Deval, who wrote the 1926 French farce Dans Sa Candeur Naïve. When the play hit Broadway in 1927 as Her Cardboard Lover, credit for the American adaptation went to Valerie Wyngate and noted humorist P.G. Wodehouse. Lonsdale, a popular British playwright at the time, was under contract with Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. Because his witty, sophisticated style perfectly matched the tone of The Cardboard Lover, his name became mistakenly credited with or added alongside Wodehouse's. This mix-up directly impacted the film adaptation of The Passionate Plumber. When MGM produced the movie, official studio records credited the story to both Jacques Deval's original French play and "the play 'Her Cardboard Lover' by Frederick Lonsdale". Consequently, decades of movie records, database listings, and film historians continue to name Lonsdale as an uncredited source writer for the Keaton film, even though Wodehouse and Wyngate were the ones who penned the English-language theatrical adaptation. According to Wikipedia, Lonsdale's contribution is that of a ghost writer, born from his close relationship with MGM and his dominance in 1930s high-society comedy theater. In the Broadway version, a woman hires a man to pose as her fake suitor to break an ailing romance. MGM acquired the rights to the play with the intention of turning it into a vehicle starring Marion Davies. The resulting pronoun trouble caused the studio to drop the Her and release it as the genderfluid The Cardboard Lover. The screenplay for the 1928 version is credited to Lucille Newmark and Carey Wilson. Then there's a third adaptation released in 1942, directed by George Cukor and starring Norma Shearer and Robert Taylor, but we’ll stick to the version at hand. 1928 was a stellar three-picture year for Marion Davies at Metro. Sandwiched between The Patsy and Show People, a pair of sparkling comedies directed by King Vidor, Robert Z. Leonard’s The Cardboard Lover, the weakest of the three, still remains a sterling example of Ms. Davies wide-ranging comedic capabilities. One of Ms. Davies specialties was her unerring habit of vamping other stars. In The Patsy she impersonated Lillian Gish, Greta Garbo, and Pola Negri. Show People found her aping Gloria Swanson and Charlie Chaplin. In The Cardboard Lover, she took to mimicking her co-star, Jetta Goudal. IMDB reports, “Goudal had hidden her real Dutch heritage and passed herself off as an exotic, elite Parisian. To maintain her fierce French persona, she stubbornly refused to speak English to the crew and would only speak French on the MGM set.” The language hurdle was a tough one for the film’s star to overcome. By way of retaliation, Ms. Davies delivered a spot-on mimicry of Goudal’s haughty affectations. (Unenamored with her behavior, Metro saw to it that this was Goudal’s one and only picture for the studio.) The film opens with a busload of 25 college girls on a continental tour, among them our lead Sally (Marion Davies), arriving in Monte Carlo via the Metro backlot. The first time we see Miss Davies, she’s so eager to see the sites — aka anyone wealthy and dressed in evening wear — she punches a hole through the bus window. Autograph snatcher Sally is determined to add another signature to her burgeoning book of inscriptions. Before it’s over, she manages to trick a famed tennis player, played by Nils Ashter, to scribble his moniker on a marriage license. At this point in his career, Robert Z. Leonard had worked with every star in the Metro firmament. As biographer I.S. Mowsis kindly put it, “Though not generally regarded by film critics as among the top echelon of Hollywood directors, Leonard nevertheless capably handled a variety of A-grade pictures.” In this case, considering his sluggish comedic timing, Leonard’s work on the picture is best described as that of a cardboard loafer. Still, I’m not one to pass up a silent film restoration, particularly one showcasing the naturally gifted comedic chops of Marion Davies. Special Features: Marion Davies: Steward of Her Legacy (2026) 9 mins. Side-By-Side Restoration Comparison 10 mins. For more information, visit Undercrank Productions.

item.title: Live Five: Sacri Monti, Chloe Lou Liddell, Thee Sacred Souls, Nights Like Thieves, Sara Petite
item.description:
Source: San Diego Reader stories Score: 3.67
August 27 Progressive psychedelic rockers Sacri Monti evoke 1970s jam bands, blending vintage organs and synthesizers with lengthy, distorted guitar improvisations set to a pounding, dance-worthy drumbeat. The band released a four-song EP on cassette with Under the Gun Records before signing with New York-based Tee Pee Records in 2015. Their self-titled debut album was recorded at Audio Design with engineer Jordan Andreen, who returned to work on their 2019 full-length Waiting Room For the Magic Hour. Their third album Retrieval dropped in 2024, and they’re reportedly working on a new full-length planned for early next year. The bill includes Encinitas-based psychedelic jam band Monarch, who will debut their new album MA3. Songwriter Sanctuary: Chloe Lou Liddell at St. Mary’s-in-the-Valley Episcopal Church August 28 Hosted by Ramona resident and local artist Cathryn Beeks in collaboration with her music and event production company Listen Local Radio, this month’s Songwriter Sanctuary showcase will feature original music “in-the-round” from three featured performers. Chloe Lou Liddell is a multi-genre songwriter and vocalist whose original band, Chloe Lou & The Liddells has been creating music reminiscent of 1960s rock ‘n soul since 2018, winning a 2020 San Diego Music Award for Best Pop Album for the debut EP Storybook. Also appearing will be a duo named Haywire and baritone vocalist Nate Donnis. Prior to the show, host Cathryn Beeks will also be sharing original music, accompanied by Laura Burdette, as part of a Pre-Show Pantry Jam. Guests are invited to enjoy music upon arrival and encouraged to contribute unopened and unexpired shelf-stable food or gently used clothing to a community pantry for under-resourced Ramona neighbors. Thee Sacred Souls at Petco Park Alex Garcia and Sal Samano (formerly of Fake Tides) began cutting bedroom demos of rhythm tracks together in 2019. Both multi-instrumentals, Alex migrated from the guitar to the drums, while Sal learned bass. The duo used Instagram to recruit City Heights singer Josh Lane, a former Sacramento music student who relocated to San Diego in 2017, to form retro soul trio Thee Sacred Souls (their name a partial nod to Chicano rock heroes Thee Midniters). After their first club date, they were signed by Daptone Records producer and co-founder Bosco Mann (Sharon Jones & The Dap-Kings), and were soon working at Mann’s Riverside studio recording tracks like “Call I Call You Rose?” which went on to top a million online plays. The group blends 1960s and 1970s R&B with elements of Chicano soul, doo-wop, and Latin R&B, creating a warm, analog sound featuring smooth vocals and deep grooves. They’ve performed on TV’s Jimmy Kimmel Live, as well as playing NPR’s famed Tiny Desk Concert series. The lineup at Petco’s Gallagher Square includes La Lom and the Womack Sisters. Nights Like Thieves at the Banshee Bar August 30 Founded in 2016, alt-pop punk band Nights Like Thieves is making music that combines upbeat and slower rhythms with emotional melodies. Founder Mario J. Rivera, who moved to San Diego after fronting Albuquerque’s Left Unsaid, formerly headed up a comedic hip-hop band named Monster Paws that was heard on TV’s Jersey Shore, The Real World, and in a Ford commercial. Citing influences such as Deftones, At the Drive In, and Sunny Day Real Estate, the debut Nights Like Thieves EP Light the Fuse and Run came out in 2017 via La Escalera Records. They’ve been dropping new releases this year such as a digital single for their track “Shadows in the Rain” and a comedic action-packed music video for “Shut Me Up" featuring filmmaker and ad creator Jake Davis. The City Heights bill also features SoCal post-hardcore band A Face With No Name and local pop-punk group A Quiet Collapse. Sara Petite at the Belly Up Tavern September 2 Americana singer-songwriter Sara Petite was born and raised in the country near Sumner, Washington, later relocating to San Diego. Her rural youth informed her subsequent songwriting, utilizing accordion, pedal steel guitar, fiddle, banjo, and mandolin. In 2022, she won two San Diego Music Awards, for Best Country or Americana Album and Best Country or Americana Artist. Petite will debut her eighth album HerStory: Snakes, Wolves and Honky Tonk Angels, performing it live in its entirety. The show will open with a set from Sara Petite’s Americana Roundup, Honky Tonk Angels, a country revue celebrating the music and spirit of country music’s most iconic women. The showcase will feature Petite alongside Ashley E. Norton (who began her career in the Arizona music scene with folk-rock band Delcoa), Chloe Lou Liddell, Lauren Leigh, and Liz West, all delivering original songs, classic country favorites, and honky-tonk anthems in what Petite describes as a “powerhouse celebration of women in country music.”

item.title: Tours in Town: The Zac Schulze Gang and Tab Benoit, Tim Kasher, Guns 'n Roses and the Black Crowes
item.description:
Source: San Diego Reader stories Score: 3.29
The Zac Schulze Gang Tab Benoit’s Soul of the Swamp Tour hits Solana Beach with an opening act soon to embark on its own European and UK headline tour, The Zac Schulze Gang. Formed during the 2020 pandemic, the band’s music mines the swagger of blues rock pioneers such as Rory Gallagher, Dr. Feelgood, and Stevie Ray Vaughan, drawing on UK pub rock tradition with tightly crafted songs that have been honed by years of relentless touring (over 200 shows per year). Fronted by 26 year-old guitarist and vocalist Zac Schulze, alongside his drummer-brother Ben Schulze and bassist Ant Greenwell, the trio won Best Emerging Blues Band at the UK Blues Awards in 2024, followed by a Young Artist of the Year trophy in 2025. Several high profile gigs have earned them press and new fans, including an acclaimed performance at Eric Clapton’s Crossroads Guitar Festival. They recently released a music video for their track “Hellhounds On My Trail,” taken from their debut album Straight To It, which dropped this month via Ruf Records. Tim Kasher: Who’s Watching Preview Tour Tim Kasher (Cursive, The Good Life) will be performing at the screening of his new directorial effort Who’s Watching, which debuts in select theaters and on digital platforms on September 18 via Dark Sky Films. Written and directed by Kasher, the film’s plot centers around eccentric musician and aspiring filmmaker named Sampson. Obsessed with his new coworker, Krista, he secretly documents every aspect of her life in an effort to make her the subject of his latest film. As his fixation intensifies, the lines between observer and participant begin to blur, pulling him deeper into a dangerous spiral of surveillance, manipulation, and obsession. The cameras keep rolling, and the question becomes increasingly unsettling: who is really watching who? The advance screening of the film will be followed by a short acoustic set and Q&A with Kasher, who will be releasing the original motion picture soundtrack for Who’s Watching on October 23. The 13-song soundtrack was written by Kasher and is split into a side A that contains songs by Toxic Cock Syndrome (TCS), and a side B that holds the score, as well as a new Cursive song, “Wounded Animal.” TCS is a fictitious metal band featured prominently throughout the film, with the music actually recorded by Kasher (guitar and backing vocals), Isaiah Radke (vocals), Darrion Lewis (guitar), Jonah Ray (drums), and Josh Ethier (bass). Guns N’ Roses and the Black Crowes When the reunited Axl, Slash, and Duff took the big stage at Qualcomm Stadium on August 2016 to play a Guns N’ Roses show for around 50,000 fans (their first time in this city since early 1992), few could have guessed that the once famously volatile lineup would still be steamrolling through stadiums a decade later. They were back in 2017 at the 8000-seat Pechanga Arena (not quite selling out the venue), and then they played to around 26,000 people at Snapdragon Stadium in 2023, a sellout crowd. The band’s most recent releases are the double-single tracks “Nothin’” and “Atlas,” which dropped digitally last December. Originating as demos from the Chinese Democracy era, the tracks were reworked by the reunited lineup featuring Axl Rose, Slash, and Duff McKagan. Opening the night will be The Black Crowes. When they played their first show in six years in 2019, the founding Robinson brothers were backed by an all-new flock of Crowes that included local Earthless guitarist Isaiah Mitchell, who also played several classic tracks with the group during an appearance on Howard Stern's SiriusXM show. Though Mitchell is no longer touring with the reunited Crowes, they’ve managed to keep busy with projects like their tenth studio album A Pound of Feathers, released in May.

item.title: 10 Best Windbreakers and Wind Shirts of 2026
item.description:
Source: Sectionhiker.com Score: 4.14
Windbreakers, wind shirts, or wind shells are ultralight jackets, running shells, pullovers, or anoraks weighing 2 to 5 ounces that trail runners, hikers, and backpackers wear to block wind and prevent it from stripping away body heat. They’re usually made of highly breathable, thin (low-denier) nylon and can be worn over a fleece or base layer to block wind and keep you warmer while hiking or trail running. They're amazingly warm, considering how lightweight they are. Here are the best windbreakers and wind shirts available today. Note: when shopping for windbreakers and wind shells, retailers may list them under trail running jackets or running jackets since there’s so much overlap with hiking and backpacking. | Item | Weight | Price | |---|---|---| | Patagonia Airshed Pro Hoodie | 3.7 oz /105g | $139 | | Patagonia Houdini Jacket | 3.7 oz /105g | $119 | | Enlightened Equipment Copperfield Wind Shirt | 2.05 oz / 58g | $120 | | Mammut Aenergy WB Hooded Jacket | 4.7 oz / 132g | $149 | | Katabatic Gear Crest Windshell | 1.8 oz / 51g | $129 | | Rab Vital Windshell Hoody | 4.6 oz /160g | $100 | | Montbell Hooded Tachyon Jacket | 2.5 oz / 71 g | $130 | | Mountain Hardwear Kor Airshell Hoody | 4.7 oz /133g | $165 | | Arc'teryx Squamish Hoody | 5.3 oz /150g | $200 | | Black Diamond Distance Wind Shell | 3.2 oz/91g | $199 | 1. Patagonia Airshed Pro Pullover 2. Patagonia Houdini Jacket 3. Enlightened Equipment Copperfield Wind Shirt 4. Mammut Aenergy WB Hooded Jacket 5. Katabatic Gear Crest Windshell 6. Rab Vital Hoody 7. Montbell Tachyon Hooded Wind Jacket 8. Mountain Hardwear Kor Airshell Hoody 9. Arc'teryx Squamish Hoody 10. Black Diamond Distance Wind Shell Windbreaker and Wind Shirt Buyers Guide Here are the key features and factors to watch for when choosing a windbreaker or wind shirt. Wind Resistance A windbreaker's wind resistance depends on how tightly the fabric is woven and on features that seal the jacket from drafts, like elastic wrist cuffs, a drawcord hem, and a fully adjustable hood. Most windbreakers and wind shirts are made from thin, low-denier nylon or polyester that is highly breathable and windproof. Some windbreakers are cut slim, which is good for running, while others are more generously sized so you can wear them over a mid-layer, which is often desirable for hiking, backpacking, climbing, and mountaineering. Breathability and Venting Unlike rain jackets, nylon windbreakers and wind shells usually have quite good breathability right through the fabric, which you can verify when you feel the fabric becoming damp under your armpits from perspiration. In general, the thinner the fabric weight, measured in denier, the better it will be for breathability. Keep in mind that very thin fabrics wear out much more quickly than thicker, more durable ones. Some jackets also use more specialized nylon with a very tight weave for improved wind resistance, though this can mean they retain more heat. If heat buildup is a concern, choose a wind jacket with a full-length zipper instead of relying on underarm vents for extra ventilation. Skipping a hood is another way to reduce a wind jacket's heat retention. Weight and Packability Wind shells typically range in weight from 1.5 oz up to 6 oz and are highly packable, usually compressing down to the size of an apple because they're made with such lightweight nylon. When hiking and backpacking, it's often convenient to stuff a wind shirt or wind jacket loosely in your backpack, filling in the voids between stuff sacks and gear, rather than scrunching it up or stuffing it into its chest pocket, unless you want to attach it to a climbing harness. Water Resistance Most windbreakers and wind shells have a DWR coating on the exterior to repel mist and drizzle, but you shouldn't count on a wind jacket to keep you dry in the rain. The DWR coating will also quickly wear off the more times you stuff the jacket into a backpack or into a pocket, rendering it useless. If you need a rain jacket, buy a proper one designed for that task. Similarly, most rain jackets are too warm to use as windbreakers. Wind Jackets vs Pullovers Windbreakers are available as jackets with full-length front zippers or pullovers with quarter-length or half-length chest zips. Full zip jackets are usually preferable in terms of ventilation because they allow more airflow, but pullovers are usually lighter because they forego the added zipper weight or are hoodless. Hood Adjustability An adjustable hood is important to seal out drafts, particularly around the face. Look for jackets with neck toggles and barring that, ones with tightly fitting elasticated face openings. A rear volume adjuster is also beneficial to downsize a hood to a human-friendly size if it's helmet-compatible. Fabric Denier Fabric denier is a unit of measurement used to determine the fiber thickness of individual threads used in the creation of fabrics. Fabrics with a high denier count tend to be thick, sturdy, durable, and heavier. Fabrics with a low denier count tend to be sheer, soft, silky, and lighter in weight. Venting While venting, as in pit zips is helpful, it's just not as effective as a full-length zipper. Because weight is at such a premium on wind shirts, if there are pit zips, they'll be permanently open rather than having zippers. Help us continue to test and write unsponsored and independent gear reviews, hiking and backpacking FAQs, and free hiking guides. I have been using Seadon’s Gale VS Jacket ever since I backed it on Kickstarter. It is only 3.5oz but has a lot of features that actually make it quite useful on the trail. It’s not as light as the wind jackets by Enlightened Equipment or Montbell, but it’s also not as expensive.

item.title: Review: REI Screeline Polartec Alpha Hoodie
item.description:
Source: Sectionhiker.com Score: 3.98
The REI Screeline Polartec Alpha Hoodie ($99) is a great value. It's a simple but well-made pullover fleece hoodie that's highly breathable and provides an amazing amount of warmth for its weight. It's the perfect companion for a windbreaker this autumn or a thicker rain jacket in winter. - Gender: Men's (women's available in much better colors) - Material: Polartec Alpha Direct Fleece (90 gsm) - Weight: Men's Large (5.3 oz) - Fit: Relaxed (semi-fitted) - Features: Scuba hood, flat-seamed to prevent chafing, thumbloops, raglan sleeve, locker loop Polartec Alpha has swept the cottage and ultralight backpacking gear scene over the past two years, and at least a dozen small companies make fleece hoodies with it: Garage Grown Gear has a good hoodie selection from many of these smaller companies, though they're often sold out because they're so popular. I think it's a good thing for the industry that REI has introduced its own fleece hoodie, and that it will boost these smaller companies because REI will educate a much larger audience about Polartec Alpha's benefits. REI's basic hoodie will spur people to look for hoodies with more features, such as chest zippers for better ventilation or kangaroo pockets. In other words, everyone's boats will float higher. Polartec Alpha (technically Polartec Alpha Direct) is an innovative insulation fabric developed by Polartec, originally designed for the U.S. military to provide breathable warmth during high-intensity activities. It began with the need for insulation that actively regulates temperature while allowing moisture to escape, unlike traditional synthetic or down insulation, which traps heat but restricts airflow. This technology uses continuous filament insulation to create a mesh core of warmth without overheating, making it highly breathable. The REI Screeline Polartec Alpha Hoodie uses 90 gsm (grams per square meter) material. This is the sweet spot for backpacking and will keep you warm down into the low 40s Fahrenheit when worn under a windbreaker. Polartec Alpha has a gauzy texture and poor wind resistance, but it traps warmth effectively when paired with wind protection. At warmer temperatures, you can wear it on its own, and it will provide the equivalent warmth of a 100 wt fleece. Polartec Alpha hoodies also come in 60 gsm and 120 gsm materials for warmer and much colder temperatures. Another benefit of Polartec Alpha is its incredible breathability. It's great active insulation because it vents water vapor (which otherwise condenses into sweat) so efficiently. Its open weave (see above) also traps warm air, especially when used with a windproof shell. Made with Polartec Fleece, its thin fibers don't absorb water, making it ideal for activities where you perspire and need a garment whose warmth doesn't degrade because it absorbs water. Comfort and Fit There's a lot to like about REI Screenline Hoodie. It has a fitted scuba hood that hugs your head without the need for a drawstring. All seams are flat-seamed for comfort and to eliminate chafing. It's semi-fitted so the fit is relaxed without constricting your torso. Elastic thumbloops are hidden in the sleeves, so they don't bunch up when you pull on a jacket. I reach for my Screeline whenever I feel a chill; it's perfect for camping, and I often wear mine to sleep in a tent. Final Verdict The REI Screeline Polartec Alpha Hoodie is an excellent value at $99, offering an impressive combination of warmth, breathability, low weight, and comfort. Its 90 gsm Polartec Alpha Direct fleece provides reliable insulation without overheating, while the relaxed fit, flat seams, thumbloops, and fitted hood make it comfortable for hiking, backpacking, camping, and everyday wear. This hoodie is highly recommended for anyone seeking a lightweight, versatile, and quick-drying layer. It works well on its own in cool weather and pairs easily with a windbreaker or rain shell when additional warmth is needed. For its price and performance, the Screeline is an outstanding introduction to Polartec Alpha insulation. SectionHiker never accepts payment for gear reviews or editorial coverage. item.title: Hugging Face is selling a cute $399 open source duck robot, Microduck
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Score: 7.05
Hugging Face unveiled the Microduck on Thursday, a cute little duck-like robot that sells for $399 — and ships before Christmas. Clem Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face, said the Microduck is an “open-source robot you can teach new tricks with reinforcement learning.” The 25-centimeter-tall duck can waddle, pick things up with its beak (up to 800 grams), get back up when it falls, crouch, and even roller skate. “Welcome to the era of open-source affordable robots to democratize physical AI and world models!” Delangue said. Hugging Face is best known as a platform and community where developers go for open model weights. However, the company acquired French startup Pollen Robotics in April 2025 to build affordable, open source AI hardware. A couple of months later, the two launched Reachy Mini, a small desktop robot. Today, they sell the $499 Reachy Mini, which is powered by a Raspberry Pi computer, and the $399 Reachy Mini Lite, powered by a Mac or PC. The new Microduck perceives the world with a camera, lidar sensors, and two IMUs (inertial measurement units that measure and report an object’s movement). Pollen Robotics noted that the Microduck’s behaviors can be trained in simulation and directly deployed on the robot. Developers can then fine-tune the bot, retrain it, and redeploy it. The SDK (software development kit), simulation, and full RL training stack are available on GitHub. For those who might find it concerning to have a robot with a camera in their bedrooms and private spaces, Delangue previously told TechCrunch that bots run by open source models are much better from a privacy standpoint than “a black box system” controlled by a few organizations, “especially if these organizations’ CEO is not the most stable person in the world.” While open source gives developers auditability and control, it doesn’t provide a guarantee that sensitive data remains private after consumers start installing software applications on top of the model. Those apps can access the bot’s cameras and microphones and, depending on how they’re built, send that data to external services. The launch of the Microduck comes as Hugging Face is reportedly set to be acquired by Nvidia at a $13 billion valuation. Nvidia and Hugging Face have been partners for years, with Nvidia providing the startup’s infrastructure since at least 2023. Both companies have also been publicly aligned in promoting open source AI. Hugging Face was recently in the headlines over a cybersecurity incident that occurred after OpenAI’s systems breached its sandbox during safety testing and hacked into the platform’s servers. TechCrunch has reached out to Hugging Face and Pollen Robotics for more information.

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and 100 other companies call for action to defend against rogue AI
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Score: 6.89
Over a hundred tech companies — including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft — have signed an open letter urging both the private and public sectors to work together to defend themselves from AI-related cyber threats. The letter — which was also signed by prominent cyber firms like CrowdStrike, Okta, and Fortinet, as well as prominent financial institutions and internet infrastructure firms — calls for the adoption of new forms of cyber defense, while also encouraging governments at the “local, national, and international levels” to collaborate on security. “In the coming months, AI-enabled cyber attacks will become far more widespread and sophisticated as models around the world become increasingly capable,” the letter states. “The companies and public services our communities depend on — from hospitals to water treatment plants to the infrastructure that powers the internet — are at risk.” The problem AI poses to traditional cybersecurity defenses has been thrust into the spotlight lately by a string of bizarre incidents in which AI agents have attacked companies. The Hugging Face incident — in which one of OpenAI’s agents autonomously broke out of its sandboxed environment and attacked the tech company — has been followed by a trail of other reported break-ins involving agents developed by other AI companies, including Anthropic and Meta. These incidents have bolstered the argument that the field of cybersecurity has been fundamentally altered and that bold new commercial solutions are necessary to mitigate them. The letter further suggests the mobilization of a “collective response,” one in which “new partnerships” are formed “to raise security standards and find new solutions to emerging cyber threats.” Several of the AI companies that have signed the letter are still actively developing ever more advanced AI models, highlighting their conflicted position. At the same time, they are also offering programs to use frontier AI models for defensive purposes, including OpenAI’s Daybreak program, Anthropic’s Mythos, and Microsoft’s new cyber platform Perception.

item.title: ATF declares ‘major incident’ as ransomware gang claims hack
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Score: 6.21
The U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, or ATF, says a cyberattack on one of its systems has been declared a “major incident,” a formal, legally defined classification that prompts a formal notification to lawmakers in Congress. ATF said in a statement that it’s responding to the cyberattack on a stand-alone system that’s separate from the bureau’s network. An ATF spokesperson told reporters that the targeted computer system contained information such as the “targets of ATF investigations.” TechCrunch has seen a claim of responsibility by the Qilin ransomware gang on its leak site, but it did not provide evidence for its claim, such as a sample of leaked data. Qilin is known for running a “ransomware-as-a-service” operation, in which it leases its hacking tools to other criminal affiliates for a cut of the profits. The gang has listed media giant Lee Enterprises and U.K. pathology lab giant Synnovis as targets. Under federal law, “major incidents” include significant cyber incidents that are likely to cause demonstrable harm to U.S. national security or broader U.S. interests. Agencies are required to disclose major incidents to Congress within a week of their discovery. The ATF joins several government agencies in recent years that have declared major incidents following a breach, including a 2023 ransomware attack on a system used by the U.S. Marshals Service, and a breach of an FBI system earlier this year that exposed phone numbers of targets under surveillance by federal agents.

item.title: OpenAI to start showing ads on ChatGPT’s free and Go tiers in India
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Score: 5.89
It seems there is no escaping the ad industry. OpenAI said on Thursday that it will start showing ads on its ChatGPT Free and Go subscription tiers in India. The move comes after the company changed its terms of service earlier this month to indicate that it will show ads to users while they use the AI assistant. OpenAI said in February that it has more than 100 million weekly active ChatGPT users in India, a huge chunk of whom are on the free or the lower-priced Go tiers. The company said on Wednesday it will start by showing ads for 50 brands and that it has partnered with agencies WPP and Omnicom for this. OpenAI will also launch an ad manager next month that will let marketers create campaigns for their companies, provided their campaigns have a daily minimum budget of ₹725 ($7.60). “With ChatGPT Ads, businesses of every size can introduce themselves at relevant, high-context moments when decisions are beginning to take shape,” Dave Dugan, head of global ads solutions at OpenAI, said in a statement. OpenAI has worked hard to cultivate its user base in India, launching a sub-$5 plan for ChatGPT Go in August 2025 and even running a limited promo that made that tier free for a full year. It also heavily advertised its products during sports tournaments, like the Women’s Premier League (WPL) and the Indian Premier League (IPL) cricket leagues. More recently, it hired Uber’s India head to lead its expansion efforts in the country. The AI lab started showing ads to U.S. users in February and expanded the program to serve ads in Europe earlier this month. Ahead of a potential IPO, expected this year or next, OpenAI has been trying to ramp up and cement its revenue sources. According to The Wall Street Journal, the AI lab recorded revenue of $6.7 billion in the second quarter ended June 2026, up from $5.7 billion the previous quarter. Last November, The Information reported that OpenAI was aiming to reach 220 million paying subscribers by 2030. The report said that at that time, 35 million users paid for its Plus and Pro plans.

item.title: Amazon just tripled its order of Nvidia chips over ‘surging demand’
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Score: 5.53
Amazon and Nvidia just got a lot closer. The two companies announced Wednesday an expanded partnership that includes a deal to add another 2 million Nvidia GPU chips to Amazon’s data centers. These GPUs, which are designed to handle the heavy compute demands of training and running AI models, include Nvidia Blackwell Ultra, Rubin, and Rubin Ultra GPUs. The chips will head to Amazon Web Services’ data centers in 2027 and 2028. The announcement, made during Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call, comes just five months after Amazon agreed to deploy more than 1 million Nvidia GPUs across AWS infrastructure starting this year. Nvidia said in a statement that since then, “demand has exceeded those expectations.” Neither company shared financial terms. It’s unclear what the exact return will be for Nvidia. But considering GPU unit costs, the deal is worth tens of billions of dollars. The announcement is notable not just because of its size and the speed in which it grew, but also because it extends beyond Amazon buying more Nvidia chips. And it’s happening even as Amazon invests in its own potentially competing AI chips. Nvidia said Wednesday that its technology, including the networking hardware that connects thousands of GPUs into one system, as well as its open models, CPUs, data processing software, and robotics platform, will also be integrated across AWS. The companies said “surging demand” from startups, enterprises, AI labs, and even governments influenced the decision to work more closely. The expanded partnership comes as Amazon ramps up its own AI chip efforts — particularly with CPUs, which are the general-purpose processors at the heart of servers. Amazon has been building its own chips to lessen its dependence on Nvidia and even compete with the chip giant. Amazon’s AI chief, Peter DeSantis, has said that AWS is in talks to sell its Trainium chips — which are a direct alternative to Nvidia’s H100 or Blackwell chips for deep learning workloads — to other companies for use in data centers. Amazon’s Arm-built Graviton CPU is also seen as a challenger to traditional server chips from Intel and AMD. Amazon has said its custom chip business is growing, noting on its last earnings call that it crossed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, driven by $225 billion in total commitments from AI labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. But it seems Nvidia is still the GOAT in the world of AI chips. With the 2 million GPU chips Amazon is adding to AWS starting in the third quarter, Nvidia also plans to send an unspecified number of Vera CPUs, “some integrated with Rubin, others standalone,” according to Nvidia CFO Colette Kress. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has big plans for the company’s Vera CPUs, boasting back in May that he had found a “brand-new $200 billion TAM” for the company. Aside from AWS, Kress said Wednesday that Nvidia expects Vera to be deployed by “every major hyperscaler, neocloud, AI lab, and system OEM, with shipments already underway to our lead partners,” which include Oracle and SpaceXAI. The partnership is also extending to Amazon’s warehouse robots and enterprise offerings. Kress said Amazon plans to adopt Nvidia’s full physical AI stack to power its fleet of robots. The stack includes Omniverse (its simulation and digital twin platform); Cosmos (its world model platform); Isaac (its robotics development platform); and Jetson (computing hardware for robots and edge AI). This week, Nvidia also introduced a new version of Jetson, designed as a more accessible robotics computer for “entry-level edge AI.” On the enterprise side, AWS will serve Nvidia’s Nemotron family of open models on Amazon Bedrock, its managed foundation model platform, and SageMaker, its managed cloud service. Nvidia also reported Wednesday that it recorded sales of $96.2 billion for the second quarter, beating analyst estimates. Data center revenue made up the majority of Nvidia’s sales for the quarter at $89 billion, up 117% from a year ago. Nvidia said it expects revenue to reach $108 billion in the third quarter, some of which will come from its next-gen Rubin GPUs. Nvidia said it began production shipments this quarter. Investors have been looking out for Rubin’s initial Q3 sales for signs that demand will continue into Nvidia’s next generation of hardware. Nvidia has committed $279 billion to secure supply and manufacturing capacity for current and future data-center projects, up substantially from $119 billion last quarter, as the chipmaker looks to secure memory and manufacturing capacity to meet AI demand over the next few years. That commitment includes $92 billion in projected spending for the rest of the fiscal year and another $87 billion in fiscal year 2028. “The thing that matters for the industry is that AI is now doing productive and useful work,” Huang said during Wednesday’s call. “AI is generating profitable tokens … If we had more compute, we could generate more profitable tokens, which results in more profit for all of the services. This is the exact phase where we’re at, which is the reason why everybody’s leaning in.” Investors will be watching to see if additional compute indeed translates so neatly into additional profits as AI companies pour hundreds of billions of dollars into infrastructure.

item.title: Meta’s $18B child-safety deal hinges on age-verification tech that doesn’t work well
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Score: 5.52
Meta reached an $18 billion settlement on Wednesday over a lawsuit brought by 29 U.S. states concerning children’s safety. The settlement is historic in scale as Meta agrees with a group of 52 attorneys general to implement sweeping changes to how minors use Instagram and Facebook. The settlement “gives the AGs what they want, which is the political story that they’ve extracted a huge amount of benefit for the public from this settlement, including the platform changes,” Jessica Nall, a technology litigator at Withers, told TechCrunch. But Nall noted the settlement’s real-dollar impact is softer than the headline number suggests. “The fact that it’s being paid over 10 years really does blunt the financial impact of the large number, especially compared to Meta’s annual revenue … We’re talking about one of these tech companies where their annual revenue is larger than the GDP of most European countries.” Indeed, Meta reported more than $200 billion in total revenue in 2025, which puts the $18 billion price tag in perspective. But the bigger story here isn’t the dollar amount. It’s what Meta now has to build: the most detailed child-safety rules any major platform has agreed to, resting on age-verification technology that still doesn’t work particularly well. Meta hasn’t admitted wrongdoing, even as it settles allegations that it intentionally designed its platforms to keep children hooked — a common tactic for companies looking to avoid a jury trial, where the risk of a worse outcome is higher.
